name: Suba (Retired)
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: Simbiti resembles Kuria in that the TBU is the mora and moras are counted in assigning melodic tones (Marlo, Mwita & Paster 2015). [...] In Simbiti and Ikizu, melodic Hs are shifted from the utterance-final syllable to the penult [...] Simbiti nouns all have a H on the first syllable of the stem, except for a handful of CVVCV-shape nouns that have a H on the noun class prefix in addition to the stem-initial H (10). [...] All six languages lack lexical tonal contrast in the verb stem. In Ikoma (12), Kabwa (13), and Simbiti (14), all verb stems in the Infinitive have a H on the first syllable of the macrostem [...]; in Simbiti the H is retracted to the prefix with monosyllabic macrostems.

new_statements.rule_in_words: For the Tanzanian half of retired [suh] (Simbiti, ssc): a restricted H-vs-toneless tone system, not word stress. The mora is the tone-bearing unit; verbs take melodic H tones placed by counting moras of the macrostem (3rd; 1st+4th; 1st; 4th), infinitives have H on the macrostem-initial syllable, nouns have H on the stem-initial syllable (a few CVVCV nouns add a prefix H), and an utterance-final melodic H retracts to the penult. The chapter makes no word-stress claim for Simbiti (regular penultimate stress is reported only for some Zanaki speakers). Nothing first-hand was found for the Kenyan half (Olusuba, sxb).
new_statements.exceptions: A handful of CVVCV nouns carry an additional H on the class prefix (ɛ̀kɛ́-mɔ́ɔ́ɾì 'calf'); H retracts to the prefix with monosyllabic infinitive macrostems; within a bimoraic syllable a melodic H spreads to the other mora to avoid contours; tones cited are phrase-medial unless stated.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level lexical/grammatical tone with an utterance-level adjustment (final H -> penult utterance-finally). Statement covers Simbiti proper only ('All data for [ssc].. is for Simbiti', Walker 2013: fn. on p. 27); it says nothing about Kenyan Suba [sxb], the other referent of the retired code.
new_statements.identity_note: suba1254 is not a language: it is Glottolog's Bookkeeping entry for ISO 639-3 [suh] 'Suba', retired 2008-01-14 and split into [sxb] Suba of Kenya (Glottolog suba1238; Olusuba/Abasuba, Mfangano-Rusinga-Kaksingri-Gwasi) and [ssc] Suba-Simbiti of Tanzania (Glottolog suba1252; Simbiti, Hacha, Surwa, Sweta, Kine, Kiroba..). Both successors are already separate keys in suba1238, suba1252, both no source found in the earlier scan). The quoted statement describes Simbiti proper (suba1252) only; nothing first-hand on prosody was obtainable for Kenyan Suba (suba1238). Any catalog entry should be filed under the successor glottocodes, never under suba1254.

sources.locator: Sec. 2.3 'Tone and syllable structure' (author final draft pp. 7-10 incl. Helda cover page; published chapter pp. 501-532)
sources.note: Sec. 2.3: Simbiti [ssc] is tonal (H vs. toneless), TBU = mora, melodic H tones assigned by mora count (3rd mora; 1st+4th; 1st; 4th of macrostem); utterance-final melodic H shifts to the penult; all nouns carry H on stem-initial syllable; infinitives H on first syllable of macrostem. No word-stress statement for Simbiti (penultimate stress is reported only for some Zanaki speakers).
